title: Galactosaemia
summary: Galactosaemia means the body cannot break down galactose, a sugar found in milk, including breast milk. Without treatment it can make a newborn baby very unwell.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the GALT gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A baby with two changed copies has galactosaemia. It is managed by removing galactose from the diet from early on, with ongoing care from a specialist team.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has galactosaemia. Could I be a carrier?
What does a test for the GALT gene involve?
card_summary: The body can't break down a sugar found in milk. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Managed with a galactose-free diet and specialist care.
care: Specialist metabolic clinics, dietitians, genetic counselling and family support groups.
